name: Shebaniah
overview: Shebaniah is a male Levite mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as one of the individuals named on the sealed document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27. He is uniquely identified as the second Levite bearing the name Shebaniah within this specific list, appearing in verses 10 and 12. His mention underscores his role within the Levitical community during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Shebaniah appears once in the biblical record provided and has no specific meaning or divine origin noted. It is presented simply as a proper name without additional explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Shebaniah as a descendant of Levi, confirming his tribal affiliation and priestly lineage. Beyond this, no other familial relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shebaniah's significance lies in his inclusion among the Levites who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah 10, reflecting his participation in the communal commitment to uphold God's law after the return from exile. Being the second Levite named Shebaniah in this document highlights the presence of multiple individuals of the same name within the Levitical ranks, emphasizing the importance of the tribe of Levi in the restoration of worship and covenant fidelity during this era.
